observation_basis: Supplemental physical observations during this same second review; no independent asset identity or separate blind verification conferred.

evidence: The narrow residential road can be located continuously between fixed A and B. Native inspection confirms a crown at A and deep building shadows along the lower interval conceal portions of the road width; a reliable complete boundary cannot be traced. No definite blocking entity can be separated from these occlusions. The draft indeterminate verdict, null boundary and empty objects are supported.

The fixed interval follows the right-hand bridge carriageway, bounded by the central divider and outer curb. Both edges and endpoint cross-sections are visible in overlapping native crops. A blue ordinary vehicle near A is present, but its blocking relationship remains unresolved; no debris or vegetation obstruction is resolved. Retain indeterminate and empty objects, and add a simple polygon following the clearly visible full carriageway.

The fixed alley and both endpoints are identifiable among the roofs. Native inspection confirms the crown over the upper bend and deep shadows along much of the lower straight segment obscure road edges and contents. No complete road polygon or definite ground-level vegetation obstruction can be established. Accept the draft with indeterminate, null target boundary and no objects.

The fixed residential road is distinct from adjoining parking forecourts. Native crops show the red ordinary vehicle in the middle/lower interval and the crown over part of the B-side road edge. That hidden edge prevents reliable full-width delineation; the vehicle blocking relationship is also unknown. Cable shadows and cracks are not physical obstruction entities. The draft is supported without changes.

The locating interval runs through a narrow dark roof gap, with limited ground detail at its B-side connection. Native inspection cannot establish continuous exposed road pavement, full ground-level width or entities within the shadow. Accept the draft indeterminate, null polygon and empty objects. Physical road presence and identity over the entire fixed interval remain unknown rather than inferred from the supplied line.

The bent residential road and its fixed endpoints are identifiable. Overlapping native crops distinguish adjoining parking courts from the main road. A small ordinary road vehicle is visible toward B, while the crown near the bend and building shadow on the opposite side obscure parts of the full cross-section. No definite blocking relationship is established. Accept the draft indeterminate, null target polygon and empty objects.

The fixed curving service road is clearly identifiable separately from the highway and the parking aisles. Native crops cover both endpoints and the bend; two tree crowns conceal portions of the garden-side road edge. Visible pavement is free of a resolved debris entity, but neither the full hidden boundary nor a ground-level vegetation obstruction can be established. Accept the draft indeterminate and null polygon without inventing the covered curb.

The fixed A-side turn, narrow main road and B junction are identifiable. Native crops distinguish the main road from house forecourts and show crowns on opposite sides obscuring portions of the middle road edges. The black ordinary vehicle near A and small road users toward B have unresolved blocking relationships. Accept indeterminate, null target boundary and no objects; visible crowns alone do not prove ground-level obstruction.
